description.narrative:
The design of the CLIPS intervention is intended to complement the EU-SCOPE PFM. There are some similar or the same activities, butthe target locations are different. This is to ensure the efficient use of available resources to achieve greater impact.
Outcome 1: Capacity and Participation Outcome statement: Strengthen the capacity of citizens and sub-national administrations to access, understand, and use budget information and digital participatory tools for effective engagement in local fiscal decision-making. Strategic Intervention: The project will build the capacity of citizens and responsive local authorities by combining structured capacity building, institutional strengthening, and digital engagement. This integrated approach simultaneously increases citizen capability,institutional readiness, and access to information. • Participate to establish a standardized and scalable capacity-building systemby working with SNAs and NCDDS to develop harmonised training manuals, facilitation tools,and a coordinated project kick-off process. This ensures consistency, quality, and alignment with national governance frameworks, creating a strong foundation for civic engagement. • Create a decentralised “community of trainers” model by pooling expertise from implementing partners and specialised organisations. This approach maximises reach without overstretchingresources and ensures that different target groups (youth, women, PwD,journalists) receive tailored, high-quality training. • Strengthen citizen capacity for informed participation through targeted training for community groups and CBOs on fiscal management, participatory budgeting, monitoring, and advocacy. This enables citizens to meaningfully influence commune and district investment planning processes. • Enhance institutional capacity of sub-national authorities (SNAs) through training on participatory public financial management, inclusive planning, and accountability. This ensures that authorities can effectively facilitate citizen engagement and integrate community priorities into decision-making. • Promote evidence-based budget advocacy and responsiveness by supporting SNAs to use budget analysis and structured dialogue to advocate for increased and more inclusive resource allocation. • Scale the use of digital participation tools through awareness campaigns on existing public financial management applications (e.g., Citizens Budget, ISAF App)
Outcome 2: Accountability and Oversight Outcome statement: Strengthen citizen-led monitoring and accountability mechanisms to track public expenditure, promote transparency, and improve government responsiveness.
Strategic Intervention: The project will operationalize accountability by shifting trained citizens from passive participants to active leaders of oversight and advocacy processes through citizen initiatives and activities that generate evidence and engage directly with government platforms. • Enable citizen-led accountability through community-driven initiatives by supporting trained groups, youth networks, and CBOs to design and implement their own civic actions on budgeting, service delivery, and governance. These initiatives include participation in budget planning processes, monitoring procurement, conducting budget analysis, and producing public accountability content. • Institutionalize participatory monitoring practices by embedding community engagement in formal planning and decision-making spaces such as Commune Investment Plans (CIP), District Development Plans(DDP), and council meetings. • Generate and use evidence for advocacy and accountability through action research and monitoring reports produced by citizens and shared with sub-national authorities, strengthening data-driven dialogue and responsiveness. • Embed civic engagementculture among youth and communities by integrating civic engagement into CBO and community work plans. This includes training teachers and students, supporting school-led debates, and fostering youth-led initiatives on fiscal governance.
Outcome 3: Institutionalization and Sustainability Outcome statement: Institutionalize inclusive, transparent, and responsive mechanisms within sub-national administrations for sustained citizen participation. Strategic Intervention: The project will transition from project-driven engagement to system-level institutionalization of participatory governance. These interventions ensure that participation-related policies and practices are revised, tested, and implemented to promote effectivecivic participation in local budget/fiscal management. • Strengthen policy frameworks for civic engagement in PFM by reviewing and updating existing civic guidelines to integrate digital participatory approaches into local fiscal management systems. • Support implementation of revised policies and guidelines by SNAs, ensuring that participatory practices are embedded in routine governance processes rather than remaining ad hoc. • Facilitate structuredand recurring council–citizen dialogue mechanisms through joint learning forums where fiscal data is analyzed collaboratively, and actionable budget adjustments are identified. • Promote peer learning and replication across communes and districts through exchangevisits, documentation, and disseminationofgood practices, enabling scaling and long-term sustainability.

participating-org.narrative: Development and Partnership in Action (DPA) is a non-political, non-religious, non- partisan, non-profit making Cambodian non-governmental organization devoted to furthering community development, partnership work with Cambodian NGOs and lobbying and advocacy. DPA is the successor of CIDSE Cambodia which was established in 1979 as part of the larger CIDSE CLV programme created by a consortiumof International NGOs from Europe, Canada, Australia and New Zealand. With a mission spanning more than 25 years,the milestones andachievements of CIDSE Cambodia are significant, not least of which is moving from meeting basic daily needs of beneficiaries to focusing on strategic long-term aims of building capacity and empowering partner organizations to assist in changing their target communities lives. CIDSE Cambodia began funding CNGOS in 1993 and formally established the Partnership Programme in 1994. Due to the evolving social climate and the strong capacity and commitment of its local staff, CIDSE Cambodia decided to localize and in 1996 began a transition process which enabled the organization to emerge as DPA in January 2006. DPA assumed responsibility for all work of CIDSE Cambodia from 1 January 2006, with an emphasis on community organizing (CO) and rights-based (RB) strategies.
